en.definition: A support vector machine using a kernel function to separate classes in a transformed feature space.
Computer systems that perform tasks associated with intelligent behaviour, such as reasoning, learning, and perception.
Algorithms whose performance on a task improves with data rather than through explicit programming.
Machine learning built on multi-layer neural networks trained end to end.
A parameterised function composed of layered units whose weights are learned from data.
A neural network trained on large text corpora to predict and generate language.
Computational methods for analysing and generating human language.
Computational methods for deriving information from images and video.
Learning a policy of actions by maximising cumulative reward from interaction with an environment.
Learning a mapping from inputs to outputs using labelled examples.
Learning structure from data without labelled outputs.
Reusing a model trained on one task as the starting point for another.
Training a shared model across devices or sites without centralising the raw data.
A classifier that separates classes with the maximum-margin hyperplane, optionally in a kernel-induced feature space.
An ensemble of decision trees whose predictions are aggregated to reduce variance.
Iterative optimisation that updates parameters in the direction that reduces a loss function.
Computing loss gradients through a network by the chain rule, layer by layer.
A neural network using convolutional filters, suited to grid-structured data such as images.
A neural network with feedback connections for processing sequences.
A sequence model built on attention rather than recurrence.
A learned weighting that lets a model focus on relevant parts of its input.
Two networks trained in opposition: a generator producing samples and a discriminator judging them.
Generation conditioned on documents retrieved at query time rather than on parameters alone.
Designing model inputs to elicit desired behaviour without changing weights.
Continuing training of a pre-trained model on task-specific data.
Fitting training data so closely that performance on unseen data degrades.
Techniques that constrain a model to improve generalisation.
Estimating generalisation by training and testing on rotating splits of the data.
Methods that make a model's behaviour understandable to people.
Systematic, unfair skew in a system's outputs with respect to groups or attributes.
The policies and processes controlling how data is collected, stored, used, and shared.
Identifying and classifying names of people, places, organisations, and similar entities in text.
A graph of entities and typed relationships used to represent and query knowledge.
